A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RNPG/RCMDP research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H are readable and support comparison, including the substantially expanded Appendix G.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original simulations, learning curves, and runtimes for Garnet, Constrained River-Swim, Modified Frozen-Lake, and Garbage Collector.

after.justification: V3 retains the tabular experiments and adds original CartPole training and testing results in Appendix G, Figures 8–10, and Table 12.

M1.justification: RCAC already appeared in v2 Algorithm 5. V3 substantially revises its prescribed updates: both critics' nominal-target updates become selected-critic updates using robust TD targets, and an NPG actor variant is added. Algorithms 2–3 also replace smoothing-dependent transition weights with explicit normalization. The core tabular surrogate objective remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds continuous-state Cartpole-v1 with perturbed state transitions, extending evaluation beyond tabular environments. Modified Frozen-Lake and Garbage Collector were already evaluated in v2 Appendix E; their appearance in the expanded Table 1 is not new task coverage.

E2.justification: The new CartPole comparisons evaluate constrained actor-critic and robust CRPO, neither of which had reported experimental comparisons in v2, alongside EPIRC-PGS adapted to function approximation. The existing RNPG, RPPG, and EPIRC-PGS tabular comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V3 introduces a CartPole training/test protocol with deterministic initialization, clipped next-state noise, robust training parameter δ=0.04, testing perturbations uniform on [0,0.04], and safety threshold 200. Existing tabular budgets remain documented as before. New Table 11 threshold labels differ from retained hyperparameter tables, leaving any actual tabular setting revision unresolved.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a focused comparison of training versus perturbed-test behavior and ordinary versus natural actor updates. Figure 10 isolates the RCAC variants from the training comparison. The existing λ sensitivity study and KL-versus-L2 regularization analyses are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Runtime comparisons remain averages over unspecified multiple runs. Neither version supplies explicit seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or defined uncertainty estimates. The added CartPole results do not introduce a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: V3 adds best-policy returns in Table 11 and CartPole outcomes in Table 12: RCAC reports reward 494.81 and cost 177.8432, versus robust CRPO's 488.06930 and 213.473. Existing tabular plots are unchanged, but runtime entries are revised, including Garnet EPIRC-PGS at γ=0.99 from 516.23 to 316.23 seconds. RPPG's numerical runtime column is removed.

T1.justification: New Assumption 3 requires a uniform statewise minimizer of the surrogate problem and becomes a condition of Theorem 4.1 and Lemma 4.2. Appendix B revises the surrogate-policy comparison, worst-case transition argument, and evaluator-error treatment. Section 6.1 also introduces the IPM function class and robust Bellman construction for function approximation.

C1.justification: V3 makes the function approximation extension and CartPole superiority over robust CRPO explicit contributions. The introduction lowers its general speedup claims from 4×/6× to 2×/3×, while the abstract replaces those numerical claims with broader efficiency and large-state performance claims. The headline tabular rates remain, subject to the added theorem assumption.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations of CartPole failures and EPIRC-PGS scalability, and explains Assumption 2's support requirement and its non-enforcement in experiments. The previous finite-state limitation is replaced by explicit open questions about function approximation guarantees and relaxing Assumption 3. Appendix H's CRPO discussion itself was already present in v2.

D1.justification: Appendix G adds CartPole initialization, noise/clipping, perturbation settings, and training runtimes. The rewritten RCAC pseudocode omits earlier rollout and replay-buffer detail. Hardware and repository access remain unchanged. Section 6.1 and Appendix G give inconsistent instructions about which neural-network layers receive regularization.

R1.justification: V3 adds two Ghosh et al. CMDP papers, Müller's IPM paper, and Ma et al.'s concurrent rectified robust policy optimization work. It develops connections to previously cited robust actor-critic research. The broad related-work structure and the existing CRPO connection remain intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are retained. V3 updates author ordering, affiliations, acknowledgments, and local wording; adds Section 6.1; develops the Appendix G placeholder; and incorporates limitations into the expanded conclusion. This is localized restructuring rather than extensive rewriting throughout the paper.

P2.justification: V3 adds CartPole Figures 8–9, a separate display of the RCAC variants in Figure 10, and Table 12. Table 11 changes from runtimes to best-policy reward/cost comparisons, while most runtime information is consolidated into expanded Table 1 without the RPPG column. Figures 1–7 retain their plotted content.

improvement.justification: V3 develops the previously sketched RCAC extension with mathematical explanation and CartPole evidence, and explicitly states an additional theorem condition. However, new Table 11 thresholds conflict with retained settings tables, and the RCAC regularization instructions disagree across Section 6.1 and Appendix G. Algorithm 5 also prints a positive MSE-gradient critic update where v2 used descent. These unresolved issues affect feasibility interpretation and reproducibility, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
